guards.issue: NARROWED 2026-07-28: the latch collapse is CLOSED; one clause of Vambrace.cs:82-96 remains, and it is a regression of the fix. CLOSED: the port now carries both C# fields (`_triggering_card` / `_used`, sts2_rl/relics/vambrace.py:27-28), clears both on attach (:30-34), latches the triggering card and nothing else in `after_modify_block_amount` (:56-65 = Vambrace.cs:82-95), and burns the once-per-combat flag in `on_card_played` (:67-73 = Vambrace.cs:98-113, gated on the played card being the latched one and on the flag not already being set). Both hooks are really dispatched, in one arm only (no `combat_rng.is_parity` branch anywhere on this path): BlockCmd.apply collects `blk_modifiers` from the additive/multiplicative folds and calls `hooks.after_modify_block_amount(blk_modifiers, target, card)` (sts2_rl/cmds.py:223-231 -> sts2_rl/hooks.py:332-345 = CreatureCmd.cs:646 / Hook.cs:649-656), and `hooks.on_card_played` fires per play index inside `_resolve_card_play` (sts2_rl/combat.py:638-639 = CardModel.cs:1957-1959). EXECUTED 2026-07-28 from the repo root: two `BlockCmd.apply` calls carrying the SAME Evil Eye instance yield 16 then 16 (the recorded probe recorded 10 then 5 pre-campaign), and the following card's 5-block gain yields 5. WHAT REMAINS: Vambrace.cs:84-87's `modifiedAmount <= 0m` early return has NO sim analogue, and the fix REMOVED the coverage the old port had -- the previous `on_block_gained` hand-roll gated on `amount > 0`, which this record's AfterModifyingBlockAmount hook entry had mapped as covering that bail. `HookSystem.after_modify_block_amount` passes only `(target, card)` (sts2_rl/hooks.py:332-345), so the modified amount never reaches the listener and vambrace.py:63-65 latches on ANY gain Vambrace multiplied, including one whose final amount is 0; `on_card_played` then spends `_used` on it. C# runs the event unconditionally too (CreatureCmd.cs:646, before the `modifiedAmount > 0m` block at :647-650), so the guard genuinely belongs to Vambrace and cannot be waived at the dispatcher. LIVE, not dormant: NoBlockPower is ported (sts2_rl/powers.py:3898-3906, x0 for any card-sourced block on its owner) and is applied by Panic Button (sts2_rl/cards/colorless_skills.py:445-448, NoBlockPower for 2 turns). EXECUTED 2026-07-28: with NoBlockPower on the player a 5-block Defend returns 0 and `_triggering_card is card` is True (C#: no latch), and `hooks.on_card_played(card)` then sets `_used = True` (C#: `cardPlay.Card != TriggeringCard` at :104 returns, charge preserved); a plain 0-amount card gain behaves the same, after which the next real 5-block gain returns 5 where C# returns 10. A fix must thread the modified amount through `HookSystem.after_modify_block_amount` / `BlockCmd.apply`; it cannot be made inside vambrace.py. guards.what: N1: C# checks `cardSource.Owner != base.Owner` on the multiplier (Vambrace.cs:71-74) and `cardPlay.Card.Owner != base.Owner` on AfterCardPlayed (:100-103); the sim checks `target is self.player` instead (vambrace.py:32, :39)
guards.rationale: The C# clauses are card-OWNERSHIP checks and exist for multiplayer, where another player's card can trigger a block gain on a creature the relic's owner can see. The sim has exactly one player and one player-side creature (CombatState holds one player plus an enemy list), so `target is self.player` and `cardSource.Owner == Owner` coincide for every reachable case. Waived as multiplayer-only under the shared contract's exclusion, not under an unreachability claim about content. Worth flagging that the two are NOT the same predicate if a player-side minion is ever ported: C# would still double a minion's block from the owner's card, the sim would not.
